Wheelspin Episode 2

By: Hein Kaiser | Paid

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
It's a follow up on Wheelspin where a second, mirror image scam came to light, and role players who may have had more involvement than what they previously led us to believe.

Summary:
This might be the biggest vehicle fraud in South Africa, not necessarily in quantum, but in its elaborate nature and how, a bank took advantage of the scam to bump up its lending book, and ergo, its market value.

Wheelspin part 1 inspired more victims muster up courage to open up about how they were caught in a scam…. But it was not Arrie’s A and A Dealings.
This, was Ride to Own, a mirror image of Arrie’s scam, but it seems, ten times bigger, in Pretoria, with a twist.

While some of Arrie’s victims had two cars on the books, with Ride to Own, one couple is down fourteen cars, another, ten, and a singleton has nine cars that he’s got to pay for now.

Here’s the kicker – it was run by Arrie’s best friend, from the same office in Menlyn that A and A Dealings did their business.

All the cars were purchased through We Buy Cars, and so far it seems the value of the scam is around R 250m, bringing the entire scam, the sum of the whole, to almost half a billion Rand.

But where its different is that all the victims knew they were buying cars, to be rented out for 6 months at a time, as an investment.

Many cars are missing – they were stripped and resold for parts to a Pretoria West Auto Parts store, which was raided by the Hawks last week, because of course, the parts are all ‘stolen’ from brand new vehicles.

And surprise – again the majority of the vehicles were financed by Marquis.

The company has not been performing to target and, their funder, Standard Bank, had an agreement with them where its shareholding increases every time the company does not make target. It rose from 20% to 43% - meaning that the founders of Marquis’s interests kept on shrinking…. They had to make target – and A and A Dealings and Ride To Own were the perfect vehicle to bump up their lending book, to realise this.

Fired whistleblower CFO Dawn confirmed what she saw happening in her statement to the Hawks.

Marcel, who was fired for rubber stamping all the deals, wouldn’t comment when I asked him whether he might be a fall guy for a greater fraud. He hesitated and answered the same way, three times.

Yet, it seems to stand up. A conversation with implicated dealership in A and A Dealings, Cruzn Motors, implied the same.

Apart from the mirror image scam on a larger scale, it seems that an unscrupulous financial institution used the opportunity to save itself, but at the expense of Standard Bank, who stood guarantee for all their lending, too.

And believe it or not, it looks like Marquis never had insurance to cover themselves against bad deals, either, which is illegal.

Carte Blanche revisits A and A Dealings, is BIG Brother and investigates the bank that’s no victim in this saga, but rather a sideline, deliberate benefactor.

Script:


VOICE OVER SCRIPT
INTRO POKER AND BETTING “ALL IN” THEME”
VO 1

It's a high-stakes game that PLAYERS bet their futures on.... the winning hand takes the pot .... the house always wins
PAUSE
VO 2

But this isn't a poker game... it's a real-life ponzi scam, betting on fast cars...for the promise of easy money... and participants, who played the wrong hand.
YOUSHAN
Arrie sent a message out to a few of us notifying us that their bank accounts had been frozen.
VO 3

Arrie van der Berg, who did not want to speak to us, was the mastermind behind A and A Dealings, a luxury car scheme in Pretoria… that we investigated in June this year.

The rules were simple... every six months, eager motorists could have their pick of the world's most sought-after vehicles in the scheme - think Ferrari's, Aston Martins and Lamborghinis.

Cars that the scheme’s members… simply could never afford - on their salaries.
UPS MARLAYNE

I'm looking at 30 to 50 of my very good friends all driving these stunning cars and everyone saying the deals are working.
VO 4

How it worked: each member bought an expensive car through the scheme... their credit applications allegedly doctored on their behalf by people at the dealership... they signed for the vehicle and the car was placed in the luxury car pool ... A and A dealings paid all the instalments ... and the drivers could live it up in the swanky cars …riding off into the sunset.
UPS YOUSHAN
They asked me, what's my preferable car? What I want to drive? I said, If you have a mustang, I don't mind and I'll drive a mustang.
VO 5

The deal was so sweet, that some drivers bought multiple vehicles..




VO 6

But there was a catch... the cars were bought at massively inflated prices... so the banks paid A and A Dealings for the car, A and A Dealings paid the monthly installments on behalf of participants' to the financier… and then pocketed the difference.

For every vehicle the participants bought in their own name... A and A Dealings took possession of the car and placed it the pool...

But as all ponzi’s eventually do... the house of cards collapsed... leaving the participants to pay for vehicles they couldn't afford.
UPS MARLAYNE

People are not paying their bonds, trying to pay a little bit to the bank. That's about 300 people that this is going to change people's lives in a negative way forever.
VO 7

While participants were left with nothing, those who ran the scheme walked away scot free.

The House always wins.
VO 8

But that was the old scam.
GLENDA
After the Carte Blanche insert, we were approached by a number of victims that made allegations about a new scheme in the form of Ride to Own.
Investors were approached to finance the vehicles and those vehicles were then put into this ride to own scheme.
UPS SANDY
she promised me that everything is fine and it's legal and it's legit, and they've been doing it for three years.
VO 9

The new scheme was eerily similar to the A and A Dealings plot... but Arrie is not involved - this time, some vehicles in the pool would be rented out for profit... while other cars had a more sinister end destination... but we'll get to that later...
VO 10

First up... meet Tyron and Chene Venter. The attractive, friendly Pretoria couple behind the new venture called .... Ride to Own.

They have a young family, lived in a leafy Pretoria estate and at face value were the very picture of success.

But behind the veil, some say the pair were cooking up deceit....




LINK

It seemed a sure bet, no upfront investment, easy money as soon as the contract was signed.


VO 11

Here’s how Ride to Own worked.

Similar to A and A, victims needed a clean credit record and financed cars at inflated prices.

Their financial information was manipulated to get finance approved.

Ride To Own then rented out these cars, to other people, at a profit – and used THAT money to repay the bank, and give a kickback to the members for every car they’d signed for.
VO 12

All Ride to Own cars were second-hand, and people who participated didnt just sign up for one or two cars… some families ended up wagering up to eighteen cars in the scheme.

Glenda Paul is a private investigator

She was one of the first to discover Ride to Own and its uncanny similarities to A and A Dealings but, with a twist or two.
GLENDA

The new victims made allegations that A and A Dealings boss Arrie van den Berg and Tyron may have actually shared offices.
VO 13

It was Chene’s role to recruit, charm and reassure members.

When Chris, not his real name, joined Ride to Own, his personal finances were rock-bottom - but it didn’t stop Chene.
CHRIS

Well, initially they told me that they've got this thing that you that you finance vehicles on on your name for six months, and then you get 15 to 25 K per vehicle. And after six months the the vehicles settled by right to own. And then after that, you're free of it.
VO 14

In other words, Chene offered Chris an attractive opportunity to make money… and have wheels that his R 15 000 a month salary would never have allowed, had he asked a bank.

All he needed to do was sign on the dotted line, while Chene helped out with some sleight of hand.







CHRIS

She told me is that she's going to send contracts through to me and I sign it and see what we can get and how many we can get. And I said, What do you mean about how many we can get? So she said to me, There's a way they do things. And these are where they bypass certain aspects at the bank and that they bypass certain stuff.
VO 15

Simply put, it is alleged that Chene’s bypass trick saw Chris’ personal information manipulated…so the banks approved him… and his family ended up with 14 cars.

That’s right… 14 cars with repayments roughly adding up to TEN times his salary
VO 16

Most members financed 3 or 4 cars in the scheme…which added up to very lucrative business for any dealership to get their hands on.

But in this voice note, Chene explains to another member how it works.
CHENE

Ons gaan koop self die karre ons het nou ons is ons is geluise dealer by BEEP gebruik hulle non stop ons koop maklik 8 miljoen rand se karre 'n maand by hulle

So, how it works is that we go and buy the cars ourselves. We are a listed dealer at BEEP and we use them non stop. We can easily buy R8 million’s worth of cars in a month.

Ons koop die kar cash en dan kry ons ons geld terug na die bank uitbetaal het by die Dealers so so ja dis hoe dit werk

We buy the cars and then we get our money back once the bank has paid the dealers. That’s how it works.
VO 17

Tyrone and Chene worked with numerous dealerships in Pretoria
Each sold the vehicles to participants in the scheme... and profited well.

This man, Gerald Fourie is employed as a salesman at Xtreme Auto in Silverton in Pretoria. He was one of their star salesmen.

Every victim we spoke to, signed for at least one car at this dealership, and… with Gerald, who had an ace up his sleeve…. a connection that bought him profit and favour…. Tyron and Gerald are related…
LINK
A scam like this would be almost impossible to pull off without several links in the chain. What did the banks know? What did the people who arranged the finance know? And importantly, what did the sales people and the dealerships from which these cars were bought know? We're here in Pretoria at one of them. It's called Extreme. We're going to stop by for a little visit.
BONGANI

My name is Bongani. How are you? I'm from Carte Blanche. Okay.
What do you know about Ride to Own?
GERALD
Well, I've got a few finance details I made for them, and then I heard there's a scam, and that's about it.
BONGANI
You had nothing to do with the owners of the company. They aren't your cousins.
GERALD
Ja, they are, I'm related to them.
BONGANI
How many cars did you sell that went through right to own? [11:57:35][2.9]
GERALD:
I don't know. I need to pull files.
BONGANI CHASING AFTER GERALD AS HE LEAVES THE DOOR INTO THE LOT – MAYBE FADE INTO VO OVER SOME OF THE ACTION
VO 18
It wasn’t a great escape, but Gerald tried…
LINK

According to our records, at least three deals were facilitated at this dealership by Gerald There's even a Facebook post where Fourie is congratulated for being the legendary salesperson of the year by, you guessed it, Tyrone and Chene Venter.
VO 19

Then, the story takes an unexpected turn.

Earlier we said that some vehicles in the pool were rented out for profit... while others, had a more sinister destination?

Turns out, Tyrone and Chene had another business - called AV Spares.

It had a dubious connection with Ride To Own.
SANDY

[He strips vehicles for spares and then sells them.


VO 20

Sandy, also not her real name, is a former Ride to Own member who saw our broadcast.
SANDY
I know of some people who have four vehicles on their names and all four vehicles have been stripped for spares.


VO 21

Two weeks ago police raided AV spares, which was once the headquarters of the Ride to Own scheme.

But they found nothing.

The new owner of AV Spares said that he is not involved in anything.
VO 23
Tyron and Chene always rushed to finalize the car financing deals.
Victims were firmly encouraged to sign up to four financing contracts in quick succession, sometimes two days apart.
Could this point to a dangerous flaw in the financial services system?
VO 24
In car financing, an accredited Finance and Insurance or FNI staffer at a dealership assists clients with their credit applications to banks.
Andrew Marshall is the chief executive of vehicle finance house, Marquis.
ANDREW

They submit the correct vehicle information and they submit the information provided by the customer in terms of income and expenditure.
VO 25
In other words, they can manipulate anyone’s information and, in people like Chris’ case, make it possible to look as if he CAN afford a small fleet of cars.
ANDREW

So that single application that is captured by the FNI is then forwarded to whichever banks they choose to send it to so that they get a multiple number of offers.
VO 26

And this is where Tyron and Chene got clever.

They used these offers, or loan approvals, to finance MORE than one car at a time.

Andrew confirmed that while he’s never seen it done before, it’s possible.


ANDREW

We don't know where a customer's applying at different dealerships or offered it with the same car, you know, at different finance providers.
VO 27

It’s a shocking weakness of a centralised electronic process that’s meant to be bulletproof.


VO 28

And that is how millions allegedly disappeared.
VO 29
The house of cards tumbled in April this year.
And while some cars may be recovered, others have been chopped up.
The victims are bankrupt… and Tyron and Chene are living it up at the resort they bought in Mozambique.
BONGANI
How much money did you get out of all of this?
CHRIS
I got 75,000. I got 75,000. Rand.
BONGANI
And now you owe millions.
VO 30
Chene dismissed and threatened anyone who dared question the couple
CHENE VOICE NOTE
So gaan bid dan vra jy vir Liew Jesus om jou te help want jou kop raas, geen wonder jou man het jou gelos nie.
So, go and pray and ask Jesus to help you, because you are crazy. No wonder your husband left you.
Pasop vir jou seuntjie, ek sê en ek het nie hart is by sulke goed kom nie jy nie twee keer dink.
Watch out for your boys, I don't have a heart when it comes to these things, so think twice…
VO 31
Can someone be this cold?
To get some answers we called Casa Lagoa, Tyron and Chene’s Mozambican hideout.
BONGANI
[Hello. Am I speaking to Chene Venter? It is Chene. This is Bongani. I'm calling you from Carte Blanche. How are you getting you? I'm very well, thank you. Listen, when I speak to you, we've got a number of allegations surrounding you and your husband and your company.
CHENE
In fact, Jinne, just listen to me. Make very, very, very sure about your facts before posting, because you're going to get kak, I'm telling you straight.
BONGANI
I just want to ask you a few questions. Can you answer?
CHENE
Don’t need to answer you. Thank you.
BONGANI
Charming lady.
BONGANI
You're angry.
ANA
Yes. We've taken the last two months our own savings to pay for those vehicles. This month. We can't do that.
VO 32
After playing their aces, Tyron and Chene are enjoying their spoils… …..everyone else at the table, folded.


PROMOS
21 Seconds #1



VO
What if the promise of a quick buck was so seductive, that participating became irresistible?
P1011626


UPS KRISTEN - HIDDEN ID
she promised me that everything is fine and it's legal and it's legit,


VO

It wasn’t. We investigate how a handsome Pretoria couple made off with millions in an elaborate scheme that duped hundreds of people


PROMO 21 Sec # 2



VO
When opportunity knocked, victims opened the door to a nightmare of mammoth proportions.


ANA
Yes. We've taken the last two months our own savings to pay for those vehicles. This month. We can't do that.




VO
We investigate a vehicle scam that bluffed and bankrupted victims and discovered the flaw in our banking system that made it all possible.


21 SECONDS # 3



VO
A smooth talking couple, a copycat scam and hundreds of unsuspecting participants


BONGANI
How much money did you get out of all of this?
CHRIS
I got 75,000. I got 75,000. Rand.
BONGANI
And now you owe millions.


VO
Small change for the price he paid. We investigate why this bet, went wrong.


11 Seconds



VO

It’s a recipe for disaster that gave a smooth talking couple the winning hand in a giant bluff….A car scam that duped the banks and left hundreds penniless.

Details Back references from Insert in Show: Title Author Last Updated 02 July 2023 - Carte Blanche HD mihle@combinedartists.co.za 03 July 2023 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Script: VOICE OVER SCRIPT INTRO POKER AND BETTING “ALL IN” THEME” VO 1 It's a high-stakes game that PLAYERS bet their futures on.... the winning hand takes the pot .... the house always wins PAUSE VO 2 But this isn't a poker game... it's a real-life ponzi scam, betting on fast cars...for the promise of easy money... and participants, who played the wrong hand. YOUSHAN Arrie sent a message out to a few of us notifying us that their bank accounts had been frozen. VO 3 Arrie van der Berg, who did not want to speak to us, was the mastermind behind A and A Dealings, a luxury car scheme in Pretoria… that we investigated in June this year. The rules were simple... every six months, eager motorists could have their pick of the world's most sought-after vehicles in the scheme - think Ferrari's, Aston Martins and Lamborghinis. Cars that the scheme’s members… simply could never afford - on their salaries. UPS MARLAYNE I'm looking at 30 to 50 of my very good friends all driving these stunning cars and everyone saying the deals are working. VO 4 How it worked: each member bought an expensive car through the scheme... their credit applications allegedly doctored on their behalf by people at the dealership... they signed for the vehicle and the car was placed in the luxury car pool ... A and A dealings paid all the instalments ... and the drivers could live it up in the swanky cars …riding off into the sunset. UPS YOUSHAN They asked me, what's my preferable car? What I want to drive? I said, If you have a mustang, I don't mind and I'll drive a mustang. VO 5 The deal was so sweet, that some drivers bought multiple vehicles.. VO 6 But there was a catch... the cars were bought at massively inflated prices... so the banks paid A and A Dealings for the car, A and A Dealings paid the monthly installments on behalf of participants' to the financier… and then pocketed the difference. For every vehicle the participants bought in their own name... A and A Dealings took possession of the car and placed it the pool... But as all ponzi’s eventually do... the house of cards collapsed... leaving the participants to pay for vehicles they couldn't afford. UPS MARLAYNE People are not paying their bonds, trying to pay a little bit to the bank. That's about 300 people that this is going to change people's lives in a negative way forever. VO 7 While participants were left with nothing, those who ran the scheme walked away scot free. The House always wins. VO 8 But that was the old scam. GLENDA After the Carte Blanche insert, we were approached by a number of victims that made allegations about a new scheme in the form of Ride to Own. Investors were approached to finance the vehicles and those vehicles were then put into this ride to own scheme. UPS SANDY she promised me that everything is fine and it's legal and it's legit, and they've been doing it for three years. VO 9 The new scheme was eerily similar to the A and A Dealings plot... but Arrie is not involved - this time, some vehicles in the pool would be rented out for profit... while other cars had a more sinister end destination... but we'll get to that later... VO 10 First up... meet Tyron and Chene Venter. The attractive, friendly Pretoria couple behind the new venture called .... Ride to Own. They have a young family, lived in a leafy Pretoria estate and at face value were the very picture of success. But behind the veil, some say the pair were cooking up deceit.... LINK It seemed a sure bet, no upfront investment, easy money as soon as the contract was signed. VO 11 Here’s how Ride to Own worked. Similar to A and A, victims needed a clean credit record and financed cars at inflated prices. Their financial information was manipulated to get finance approved. Ride To Own then rented out these cars, to other people, at a profit – and used THAT money to repay the bank, and give a kickback to the members for every car they’d signed for. VO 12 All Ride to Own cars were second-hand, and people who participated didnt just sign up for one or two cars… some families ended up wagering up to eighteen cars in the scheme. Glenda Paul is a private investigator She was one of the first to discover Ride to Own and its uncanny similarities to A and A Dealings but, with a twist or two. GLENDA The new victims made allegations that A and A Dealings boss Arrie van den Berg and Tyron may have actually shared offices. VO 13 It was Chene’s role to recruit, charm and reassure members. When Chris, not his real name, joined Ride to Own, his personal finances were rock-bottom - but it didn’t stop Chene. CHRIS Well, initially they told me that they've got this thing that you that you finance vehicles on on your name for six months, and then you get 15 to 25 K per vehicle. And after six months the the vehicles settled by right to own. And then after that, you're free of it. VO 14 In other words, Chene offered Chris an attractive opportunity to make money… and have wheels that his R 15 000 a month salary would never have allowed, had he asked a bank. All he needed to do was sign on the dotted line, while Chene helped out with some sleight of hand. CHRIS She told me is that she's going to send contracts through to me and I sign it and see what we can get and how many we can get. And I said, What do you mean about how many we can get? So she said to me, There's a way they do things. And these are where they bypass certain aspects at the bank and that they bypass certain stuff. VO 15 Simply put, it is alleged that Chene’s bypass trick saw Chris’ personal information manipulated…so the banks approved him… and his family ended up with 14 cars. That’s right… 14 cars with repayments roughly adding up to TEN times his salary VO 16 Most members financed 3 or 4 cars in the scheme…which added up to very lucrative business for any dealership to get their hands on. But in this voice note, Chene explains to another member how it works. CHENE Ons gaan koop self die karre ons het nou ons is ons is geluise dealer by BEEP gebruik hulle non stop ons koop maklik 8 miljoen rand se karre 'n maand by hulle So, how it works is that we go and buy the cars ourselves. We are a listed dealer at BEEP and we use them non stop. We can easily buy R8 million’s worth of cars in a month. Ons koop die kar cash en dan kry ons ons geld terug na die bank uitbetaal het by die Dealers so so ja dis hoe dit werk We buy the cars and then we get our money back once the bank has paid the dealers. That’s how it works. VO 17 Tyrone and Chene worked with numerous dealerships in Pretoria Each sold the vehicles to participants in the scheme... and profited well. This man, Gerald Fourie is employed as a salesman at Xtreme Auto in Silverton in Pretoria. He was one of their star salesmen. Every victim we spoke to, signed for at least one car at this dealership, and… with Gerald, who had an ace up his sleeve…. a connection that bought him profit and favour…. Tyron and Gerald are related… LINK A scam like this would be almost impossible to pull off without several links in the chain. What did the banks know? What did the people who arranged the finance know? And importantly, what did the sales people and the dealerships from which these cars were bought know? We're here in Pretoria at one of them. It's called Extreme. We're going to stop by for a little visit. BONGANI My name is Bongani. How are you? I'm from Carte Blanche. Okay. What do you know about Ride to Own? GERALD Well, I've got a few finance details I made for them, and then I heard there's a scam, and that's about it. BONGANI You had nothing to do with the owners of the company. They aren't your cousins. GERALD Ja, they are, I'm related to them. BONGANI How many cars did you sell that went through right to own? [11:57:35][2.9] GERALD: I don't know. I need to pull files. BONGANI CHASING AFTER GERALD AS HE LEAVES THE DOOR INTO THE LOT – MAYBE FADE INTO VO OVER SOME OF THE ACTION VO 18 It wasn’t a great escape, but Gerald tried… LINK According to our records, at least three deals were facilitated at this dealership by Gerald There's even a Facebook post where Fourie is congratulated for being the legendary salesperson of the year by, you guessed it, Tyrone and Chene Venter. VO 19 Then, the story takes an unexpected turn. Earlier we said that some vehicles in the pool were rented out for profit... while others, had a more sinister destination? Turns out, Tyrone and Chene had another business - called AV Spares. It had a dubious connection with Ride To Own. SANDY [He strips vehicles for spares and then sells them. VO 20 Sandy, also not her real name, is a former Ride to Own member who saw our broadcast. SANDY I know of some people who have four vehicles on their names and all four vehicles have been stripped for spares. VO 21 Two weeks ago police raided AV spares, which was once the headquarters of the Ride to Own scheme. But they found nothing. The new owner of AV Spares said that he is not involved in anything. VO 23 Tyron and Chene always rushed to finalize the car financing deals. Victims were firmly encouraged to sign up to four financing contracts in quick succession, sometimes two days apart. Could this point to a dangerous flaw in the financial services system? VO 24 In car financing, an accredited Finance and Insurance or FNI staffer at a dealership assists clients with their credit applications to banks. Andrew Marshall is the chief executive of vehicle finance house, Marquis. ANDREW They submit the correct vehicle information and they submit the information provided by the customer in terms of income and expenditure. VO 25 In other words, they can manipulate anyone’s information and, in people like Chris’ case, make it possible to look as if he CAN afford a small fleet of cars. ANDREW So that single application that is captured by the FNI is then forwarded to whichever banks they choose to send it to so that they get a multiple number of offers. VO 26 And this is where Tyron and Chene got clever. They used these offers, or loan approvals, to finance MORE than one car at a time. Andrew confirmed that while he’s never seen it done before, it’s possible. ANDREW We don't know where a customer's applying at different dealerships or offered it with the same car, you know, at different finance providers. VO 27 It’s a shocking weakness of a centralised electronic process that’s meant to be bulletproof. VO 28 And that is how millions allegedly disappeared. VO 29 The house of cards tumbled in April this year. And while some cars may be recovered, others have been chopped up. The victims are bankrupt… and Tyron and Chene are living it up at the resort they bought in Mozambique. BONGANI How much money did you get out of all of this? CHRIS I got 75,000. I got 75,000. Rand. BONGANI And now you owe millions. VO 30 Chene dismissed and threatened anyone who dared question the couple CHENE VOICE NOTE So gaan bid dan vra jy vir Liew Jesus om jou te help want jou kop raas, geen wonder jou man het jou gelos nie. So, go and pray and ask Jesus to help you, because you are crazy. No wonder your husband left you. Pasop vir jou seuntjie, ek sê en ek het nie hart is by sulke goed kom nie jy nie twee keer dink. Watch out for your boys, I don't have a heart when it comes to these things, so think twice… VO 31 Can someone be this cold? To get some answers we called Casa Lagoa, Tyron and Chene’s Mozambican hideout. BONGANI [Hello. Am I speaking to Chene Venter? It is Chene. This is Bongani. I'm calling you from Carte Blanche. How are you getting you? I'm very well, thank you. Listen, when I speak to you, we've got a number of allegations surrounding you and your husband and your company. CHENE In fact, Jinne, just listen to me. Make very, very, very sure about your facts before posting, because you're going to get kak, I'm telling you straight. BONGANI I just want to ask you a few questions. Can you answer? CHENE Don’t need to answer you. Thank you. BONGANI Charming lady. BONGANI You're angry. ANA Yes. We've taken the last two months our own savings to pay for those vehicles. This month. We can't do that. VO 32 After playing their aces, Tyron and Chene are enjoying their spoils… …..everyone else at the table, folded. PROMOS 21 Seconds #1 VO What if the promise of a quick buck was so seductive, that participating became irresistible? P1011626 UPS KRISTEN - HIDDEN ID she promised me that everything is fine and it's legal and it's legit, VO It wasn’t. We investigate how a handsome Pretoria couple made off with millions in an elaborate scheme that duped hundreds of people PROMO 21 Sec # 2 VO When opportunity knocked, victims opened the door to a nightmare of mammoth proportions. ANA Yes. We've taken the last two months our own savings to pay for those vehicles. This month. We can't do that. VO We investigate a vehicle scam that bluffed and bankrupted victims and discovered the flaw in our banking system that made it all possible. 21 SECONDS # 3 VO A smooth talking couple, a copycat scam and hundreds of unsuspecting participants BONGANI How much money did you get out of all of this? CHRIS I got 75,000. I got 75,000. Rand. BONGANI And now you owe millions. VO Small change for the price he paid. We investigate why this bet, went wrong. 11 Seconds VO It’s a recipe for disaster that gave a smooth talking couple the winning hand in a giant bluff….A car scam that duped the banks and left hundreds penniless.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: It's a follow up on Wheelspin where a second, mirror image scam came to light, and role players who may have had more involvement than what they previously led us to believe.
metadata.Summary: This might be the biggest vehicle fraud in South Africa, not necessarily in quantum, but in its elaborate nature and how, a bank took advantage of the scam to bump up its lending book, and ergo, its market value. Wheelspin part 1 inspired more victims muster up courage to open up about how they were caught in a scam…. But it was not Arrie’s A and A Dealings. This, was Ride to Own, a mirror image of Arrie’s scam, but it seems, ten times bigger, in Pretoria, with a twist. While some of Arrie’s victims had two cars on the books, with Ride to Own, one couple is down fourteen cars, another, ten, and a singleton has nine cars that he’s got to pay for now. Here’s the kicker – it was run by Arrie’s best friend, from the same office in Menlyn that A and A Dealings did their business. All the cars were purchased through We Buy Cars, and so far it seems the value of the scam is around R 250m, bringing the entire scam, the sum of the whole, to almost half a billion Rand. But where its different is that all the victims knew they were buying cars, to be rented out for 6 months at a time, as an investment. Many cars are missing – they were stripped and resold for parts to a Pretoria West Auto Parts store, which was raided by the Hawks last week, because of course, the parts are all ‘stolen’ from brand new vehicles. And surprise – again the majority of the vehicles were financed by Marquis. The company has not been performing to target and, their funder, Standard Bank, had an agreement with them where its shareholding increases every time the company does not make target. It rose from 20% to 43% - meaning that the founders of Marquis’s interests kept on shrinking…. They had to make target – and A and A Dealings and Ride To Own were the perfect vehicle to bump up their lending book, to realise this. Fired whistleblower CFO Dawn confirmed what she saw happening in her statement to the Hawks. Marcel, who was fired for rubber stamping all the deals, wouldn’t comment when I asked him whether he might be a fall guy for a greater fraud. He hesitated and answered the same way, three times. Yet, it seems to stand up. A conversation with implicated dealership in A and A Dealings, Cruzn Motors, implied the same. Apart from the mirror image scam on a larger scale, it seems that an unscrupulous financial institution used the opportunity to save itself, but at the expense of Standard Bank, who stood guarantee for all their lending, too. And believe it or not, it looks like Marquis never had insurance to cover themselves against bad deals, either, which is illegal. Carte Blanche revisits A and A Dealings, is BIG Brother and investigates the bank that’s no victim in this saga, but rather a sideline, deliberate benefactor.
metadata.Reason for legal: It's a complex scam and it includes Marquis Finance, Wesbank, again.
